text: The sinkings of the Ivanovets, Tsezar Kunikov and Sergey Kotov are uncontested and are also counted by Oryx.
The corvette Ivanovets (Project 1241.1/12411 Tarantul-III) was sunk on the night of 31 Jan – 1 Feb 2024 near Lake Donuzlav.
Oryx lists one Mi-8 destroyed with evidence posted on the morning of 31 Dec 2024.
The research file infers from the tweet date that the Mi-8 Oryx lists as destroyed matches the 31 Dec 2024 sea-drone engagement.
notes: OUTCOME; the match is the dossier's inference from the date

text: HUR said in Jul 2024 that its Maguras alone had hit 14 ships, destroyed 8, and caused over $500m of damage.
Oryx lists 40 Russian naval ships and submarines lost to all causes over the whole war, 26 destroyed and 14 damaged, as fetched on 1 Oct 2026.
Ukraine lost its surface navy in the first days of the Russian invasion in 2022.
After losing its surface navy, Ukraine fought the Black Sea Fleet (BSF) with missiles and with uncrewed surface vessels (USVs).
Ukraine's uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) are explosive-laden, remote-controlled speedboats that ride low in the water.
The first Ukrainian sea-drone swarm raided Sevastopol bay on 29 Oct 2022 and hit the frigate Admiral Makarov and the minesweeper Ivan Golubets, but sank nothing.

observations.subject: ships sunk in the 29 Oct 2022 Sevastopol raid

text: After the 29 Oct 2022 raid, Ukraine's sea-drone programme split: the SBU built the Sea Baby, a heavy-warhead boat for static targets such as the Crimean Bridge and the Olenegorsky Gornyak in Novorossiysk.
HUR took the original sea-drone maker's design forward as the Magura V5, a smaller and faster boat than the Sea Baby, built to hunt ships at sea.
Through 2023, Ukrainian missiles and sea drones together drove most of the Black Sea Fleet from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk, with the move in October 2023.
Ukraine opened its own export corridor along the western Black Sea coast on 16 Aug 2023.
The climax of the Black Sea drone war came in Feb – Mar 2024, when HUR's Group 13 used night swarms of Magura V5s to sink three Russian ships in five weeks.

observations.subject: BSF ships sunk by Magura V5 swarms

text: HUR's Magura V5 swarm sank the corvette Ivanovets off Donuzlav on 1 Feb 2024.
HUR's Magura V5 swarm sank the landing ship Tsezar Kunikov off Alupka on 14 Feb 2024.
HUR's Magura V5 swarm sank the patrol ship Sergey Kotov off the Kerch Strait on 5 Mar 2024.
After the Feb – Mar 2024 sinkings, the Black Sea Fleet commander was sacked.
After the Feb – Mar 2024 sinkings, the Russian Navy limited its operations to the eastern Black Sea.
Russia answered the Ukrainian sea drones with helicopters, Su-30SM jets, gunboats, booms and FPV drones that hunted the drones at sea.
Ukraine responded to Russian air hunting of its sea drones by arming the drones with missiles.
On 31 Dec 2024, R-73 "SeeDragon" missiles fired from a Magura V5 downed at least one Mi-8 helicopter off Cape Tarkhankut.
HUR later claimed that two Mi-8s were downed by its Magura V5s on 31 Dec 2024.
On 2 May 2025, AIM-9M Sidewinders fired from Magura V7s downed at least one Su-30SM west of Novorossiysk.
HUR claims that its Magura V7s downed two Su-30SMs on 2 May 2025.
The landing ship Tsezar Kunikov (Project 775 Ropucha-I) was sunk on 14 Feb 2024 about 4 km off Alupka.

observations.subject: distance offshore of the Tsezar Kunikov sinking

text: The patrol ship Sergey Kotov (Project 22160) was sunk on 5 Mar 2024 near the Kerch Strait.
A Russian insider places the wreck of the Sergey Kotov 5 km off Cape Takil.

observations.subject: distance offshore of the Sergey Kotov wreck

text: Ukrainian sea drones damaged the frigate Admiral Makarov and the minesweeper Ivan Golubets at Sevastopol on 29 Oct 2022.
Ukrainian sea drones damaged the intelligence ship Ivan Khurs on 24 May 2023.
On 4 Aug 2023, Ukrainian sea drones holed the landing ship Olenegorsky Gornyak at Novorossiysk.
On 4 Aug 2023, a Ukrainian sea drone holed the tanker Sig near Kerch.
On 10 Nov 2023, Ukrainian sea drones hit the Serna and Akula landing craft off Chornomorske.
On 31 Dec 2024, HUR first claimed one Mi-8 destroyed and one damaged by its sea drones.
On 2 Jan 2025, HUR revised its 31 Dec 2024 claim to two Mi-8s destroyed and a third helicopter damaged.
The video of the 31 Dec 2024 engagement shows one helicopter hit and crashing.
HUR, the Russian milblogger Rybar and other Russian Telegram channels agree that one Su-30SM went down on 2 May 2025, and its crew was rescued by a civilian ship.
Budanov claims a second Su-30SM was downed on 2 May 2025 with its crew killed, but there is no video.
The win band for aircraft shot down by Ukrainian sea drones is one to two of each type (Mi-8 and Su-30SM).

observations.value_text: one to two of each type
observations.subject: Mi-8 and Su-30SM each

text: The strategic result of the Black Sea drone war is that the Black Sea Fleet is based at Novorossiysk and has stayed out of the western Black Sea since late 2023.
The Ukrainian corridor carried 45 Mt of cargo from Greater Odesa in about 9 months, to May 2024.
Ukraine's April 2024 seaborne exports were the highest since Feb 2022.
UK Defence Secretary Shapps said in Dec 2023 that 20% of the Black Sea Fleet had been destroyed in four months.

metric_new.label: Share of a fleet destroyed or disabled

notes: time from/to approximates 'four months' to Dec 2023

text: Ukrainian StratCom said in early Feb 2024 that about 33% of Black Sea Fleet warships had been disabled: 24 ships and 1 submarine.

metric_new.label: Share of a fleet destroyed or disabled

text: Ukrainian Navy spokesman Pletenchuk said on 6 Mar 2024 that 27 of about 80 Black Sea Fleet units had been hit, 14 destroyed and 15 damaged, and that "one third" was destroyed.

metric_new.label: Share of a fleet destroyed or disabled

notes: 14 + 15 = 29, not 27, as given in the text

text: In Jun 2024 Pletenchuk said that officially 28 Black Sea Fleet ships had been hit, plus 10 under repair.
According to Defense Express, HUR's Maguras had destroyed 9 vessels, 2 Su-30s and 2 Mi-8s by 15 May 2025.
HUR spokesman Yusov said on 15 May 2025 that Maguras had hit 21 targets, including "16 warships at the bottom", 3 helicopters and 2 jets.
A Georgetown student journal estimated in 2026 that the Black Sea Fleet had lost about 40% of its effective capability.

text: In Jun 2022, the first prototype Ukrainian sea drone, with one Starlink channel, was tested on a reservoir.
In Jul 2022, Sea Baby design work began in the SBU.
In late Jul 2022, HUR used improvised naval drones on the Dnipro in Zaporizhzhia Oblast.
In Sep 2022, Musk refused Starlink coverage around Crimea.
On the night of 16–17 Sep 2022, the first Ukrainian sea-drone mission against Sevastopol bay failed because Starlink did not work in Crimea.
In late Sep 2022, an early Ukrainian USV washed up near Sevastopol, the first public sighting of one.
At about 04:00–04:20 on 29 Oct 2022, Ukraine made the first sea-drone swarm raid on Sevastopol.
GeoConfirmed counts 6–8 USVs in the 29 Oct 2022 Sevastopol raid and at least 3 ships hit, including the Admiral Makarov.
The Russian MoD admitted "minor" damage to the minesweeper Ivan Golubets and a damaged boom in Pivdenna (Yuzhnaya) Bay after the 29 Oct 2022 raid.
Governor Razvozhaev claimed that 9 UAVs and 7 USVs took part in the 29 Oct 2022 attack on Sevastopol.
On 29 Oct 2022, Russia "suspended" its part in the Black Sea Grain Initiative and blamed British specialists in Ochakiv for the Sevastopol raid.
In Nov 2022, Ukraine announced a combat sea drone with up to 800 km range.
At the end of 2022, the SBU decided to build its own sea drones (Sea Baby), and the original maker signed with HUR (Magura).
Early on 22 Mar 2023, USVs tried to enter Sevastopol harbour: one was stopped by the boom, and two jumped it and were destroyed inside, according to a Russian naval blogger.

On 24 May 2023, at 05:30 by the Russian claim, Magura scored its first success: the intelligence ship Ivan Khurs was attacked about 120–140 km north-east of the Bosphorus after a transit of over 500 km.

observations.subject: attack position north-east of the Bosphorus

text: HUR says its drones chased the Ivan Khurs under fire from about 01:30 to 07:00 on 24 May 2023.
The Russian MoD claims all 3 USVs that attacked the Ivan Khurs on 24 May 2023 were destroyed.
The Ukrainian MoD video of the 24 May 2023 attack shows a hit near the stern of the Ivan Khurs.
On 17 Jul 2023, two Sea Babies hit the Crimean Bridge and a span collapsed.
Russia quit the Black Sea grain deal on 17 Jul 2023, the same day as the Sea Baby strike on the Crimean Bridge.
The Magura V5 was shown at IDEF in Istanbul on 25–28 Jul 2023, and CNN confirmed it was operational.
In late Jul 2023, a Magura first damaged the patrol ship Sergey Kotov at sea.
On the night of 3–4 Aug 2023 at Novorossiysk, an SBU USV with 450 kg of TNT holed the landing ship Olenegorsky Gornyak, which was listing to port under tow at dawn.
The Russian MoD reported that two USVs attacked Novorossiysk on 3–4 Aug 2023 and were "repelled".
The 3–4 Aug 2023 Novorossiysk strike was a joint SBU–Navy operation, and HUR says its Maguras also took part.
At about 23:20 on 4 Aug 2023, the tanker Sig was hit south of the Kerch Strait by a sea drone with 450 kg of explosive; its engine room flooded but it stayed afloat.
Around 12–13 Aug 2023, Ukraine started registering ships for a "temporary corridor", after Russia had said merchant ships would be treated as hostile.
On 16 Aug 2023, the Joseph Schulte, carrying 2,114 containers, left Odesa by the new corridor, the first civilian ship since the grain deal ended.
On 24 Aug 2023, Zelensky gave a combat flag to the 385th Separate Brigade, the first USV unit, with HUR and SBU operators.

mentions.name: 385th Separate Brigade of Special-Purpose Naval Unmanned Systems

text: In Aug 2023, Russia built a barricade at the Crimean Bridge against USVs.
On 14 Sep 2023, USVs damaged two Project 22160 patrol ships, the Vasily Bykov and the Sergey Kotov.
On 14 Sep 2023, a Sea Baby hit the corvette Samum.
On 22 Sep 2023, Storm Shadow missiles hit the Black Sea Fleet headquarters in Sevastopol.

Satellite imagery from 1–4 Oct 2023 shows about 14 Black Sea Fleet ships, including both Grigorovich frigates, 3 submarines, 5 large landing ships and small missile ships, moved from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk.
In Oct 2023, a Sea Baby damaged the patrol ship Pavel Derzhavin.
In Oct 2023, a USV hit the tug Professor Nikolai Muru.
On the night of 9–10 Nov 2023, Maguras hunted and hit two fast landing craft, the Serna and the Akula, in convoy off Chornomorske, HUR's first "pure hunter" success.
In Nov 2023, Russia recovered an intact Magura V5, photographed washed ashore near Sevastopol.
In Nov 2023, USVs destroyed the Kerch Bridge barricade.
In Dec 2023, a Sea Baby hit the survey ship Vladimir Kozitsky.
In Dec 2023, Naval News described Russia's layered counter-USV defence and saw at least 16 Maguras at one base.
On 26 Dec 2023, the Ukrainian Air Force destroyed the landing ship Novocherkassk at Feodosia with missiles.
On the night of 31 Jan – 1 Feb 2024, the corvette Ivanovets was sunk "on the raid of Lake Donuzlav" by Magura sea drones.

cites.quote: on the raid of Lake Donuzlav

text: The Ivanovets took six Magura hits through AK-630M fire, rolled astern and sank.
The Russian search and rescue after the sinking of the Ivanovets failed.
On 1 Feb 2024, HUR released a 128-second video of the Ivanovets strike, and Russian milbloggers confirmed the sinking.
On the night of 13–14 Feb 2024, before dawn, the landing ship Tsezar Kunikov was sunk about 4 km off Alupka with critical breaches to port.
During the 14 Feb 2024 attack, the Tsezar Kunikov's crew fired back and manoeuvred.
The Russian MoD claimed 6 USVs were downed on 14 Feb 2024.
After the Tsezar Kunikov attack, Mi-8 and Ka-27 helicopters searched off Foros–Katsiveli.
HUR says the Tsezar Kunikov was a substitute target: the convoy its drones were hunting moved hours before.
On 14 Feb 2024, Pletenchuk said 5 of 13 Black Sea Fleet landing ships remained in service, with 4 destroyed and 4 under repair.
UK Defence Intelligence reported on 15 Feb 2024 that BSF commander Adm. Viktor Sokolov had been removed, with Vice Adm. Sergei Pinchuk likely acting commander.
On 22–23 Feb 2024, a crowdfunding drive raised UAH 297.5m for 35 Sea Babies in two days.
On the night of 4–5 Mar 2024, the patrol ship Sergey Kotov was sunk near the Kerch Strait by five Magura hits to the stern and both sides.

observations.subject: Magura hits on the Sergey Kotov

text: HUR says the sinking of the Sergey Kotov killed 7 crew and wounded 6, with 52 evacuated, and cost $65m.
During the Sergey Kotov attack, the Crimean Bridge closed for more than 8 hours, reopening at about 07:00 on 5 Mar 2024.
A Russian insider said on 5 Mar 2024 that a tow of the Sergey Kotov was tried and the ship sank 5 km off Cape Takil.
After the Sergey Kotov sinking on 5 Mar 2024, Russian milbloggers attacked the command.
On 6 Mar 2024, Pletenchuk said "one third" of about 80 Black Sea Fleet units had been destroyed.
On 6 Mar 2024, the SBU showed the Sea Baby 2024 "Avdiivka", carrying almost 1 t over 1,000+ km.
In Mar 2024, Russian Navy chief Adm. Yevmenov was replaced by Adm. Moiseyev.
On 17 Mar 2024, Shoigu at the Black Sea Fleet command post ordered daily anti-USV drills and extra weapons.
From Mar 2024, Black Sea Fleet ships got black-painted bows and sterns and painted decoys.
On 19 Mar 2024, UK Defence Intelligence assessed that the Russian Navy had "highly likely" limited its operations to the eastern Black Sea.
At about 03:40 on 10 Apr 2024, an Mi-24VP of the Baltic Fleet's 396th Regiment, flying from Kacha to hunt USVs off Sevastopol, was lost with 4 crew; Russian channels said a malfunction was likely.
In early May 2024 (footage dated 6 May), the Russian MoD released footage of a Ka-29 gunning down a USV armed with R-73 rails; one missile appears to fire.
On 30 May 2024, Maguras hit four KS-701 Tunets boats in Crimea and destroyed two.
In Jun 2024, the SBU said Sea Babies had laid 15+ mines off Crimea and damaged four ships.

observations.subject: ships damaged by Sea Baby mines

text: In Jun 2024, Pletenchuk said 28 Black Sea Fleet ships had been hit, plus 10 under repair.
On 21 Jul 2024, HUR said its Maguras had caused over $500m of damage.
On 10 Aug 2024, a Magura destroyed a KS-701 Tunets near Chornomorske.
A video dated 30 Sep 2024 shows Black Sea Fleet special forces training to launch FPV drones from a helicopter against USVs.
On the night of 5–6 Dec 2024 in Kerch Bay, Sea Babies with stabilised heavy machine guns fought helicopters, a Su-30 and Raptor boats.
The SBU says helicopters were damaged and a bridge-repair barge was hit in the 5–6 Dec 2024 Kerch Bay raid.
On the night of 30–31 Dec 2024 there were explosions in Sevastopol; Razvozhayev claimed 4 aerial and 2 naval drones were repelled.
On 31 Dec 2024 off Cape Tarkhankut, Group 13 Maguras armed with R-73 "SeeDragon" missiles downed an Mi-8 under fire from the helicopters; a second Mi-8 was hit and reached its airfield.
HUR called the 31 Dec 2024 Mi-8 shootdown the first air kill by a sea drone.
On 2 Jan 2025, HUR revised its claim to two Mi-8s destroyed and a third helicopter damaged.
In Jan 2025, HUR began fitting AIM-9 Sidewinders to sea drones.
On 2 May 2025 (ISW dates it 3 May), about 50 km west of Novorossiysk, three Magura V7s, two of them firing, downed a Su-30SM with AIM-9s.
The crew of the Su-30SM downed on 2 May 2025 ejected and was picked up by a civilian ship.
Budanov claims a second Su-30 was downed on 2 May 2025 with its crew killed; there is no video.
On the night of 2–3 May 2025, Ukraine made a combined drone, missile and USV strike on Novorossiysk.
The Russian MoD claims 170 drones, 11 missiles and 14 sea drones were destroyed on the night of 2–3 May 2025.
On 15 May 2025, HUR unveiled the Magura V7 in Kyiv and gave its tallies: 9 vessels, 2 Su-30s and 2 Mi-8s, or 21 targets.
The northern Black Sea spans about 600 km great-circle from the Odesa coast to Novorossiysk, with Crimea in the middle.
The Russian Black Sea Fleet bases, anchorages and helicopter fields line Crimea's west and south coasts and the Caucasus shore; Ukrainian sea drones start off the north-west coast.
Distances between the Black Sea locations in the dossier are great-circle distances computed from OSM points; real routes by sea are longer.
HUR's sea-drone route to the Sergey Kotov was about 800 km.

observations.subject: sea route to the Sergey Kotov

text: Odesa, at 46.484, 30.732 (lat, lon), holds Ukrainian ports and is the likely launch region for Ukraine's sea drones.
Greater Odesa comprises the ports of Odesa, Chornomorsk and Pivdenne; Chornomorsk is at 46.301, 30.655.
Pivdenne, one of the Greater Odesa ports, is at 46.623, 31.099.
Russia blamed Ochakiv (46.615, 31.545) as the launch site of the 2022 sea-drone attack, claiming "British specialists" were there.
Zmiinyi Island (Snake Island), at 45.255, 30.203, is the north-western marker of the Black Sea diorama, 275 km from Sevastopol Bay.

observations.subject: Zmiinyi Island to Sevastopol Bay, great-circle

text: Sevastopol Bay, at 44.613, 33.579, is the Black Sea Fleet's main base, the scene of the 2022 swarm raid and protected by booms; it is 304 km from Odesa.
A boom in Pivdenna (Yuzhnaya) Bay, at 44.615, 33.529, was damaged on 29 Oct 2022.
Kacha airfield, at 44.781, 33.565, is a Russian naval helicopter base; the Mi-24VP lost in Apr 2024 flew from there.
Lake Donuzlav, with the town of Novoozerne at 45.384, 33.117 (the lake is OSM relations 9505344/5), is a Russian naval anchorage and the site of the Ivanovets "raid", 221 km from Odesa.
Chornomorske, at 45.506, 32.683, is a Russian navy point where Maguras hit the Serna and Akula (Nov 2023) and a KS-701 (Aug 2024).
Cape Tarkhankut, at 45.347, 32.494, is the site of the 31 Dec 2024 Mi-8 shootdown, 186 km from Odesa and 118 km from Sevastopol Bay.

observations.subject: Cape Tarkhankut to Sevastopol Bay, great-circle

text: Katsiveli, on Crimea's south coast near Alupka, is at 44.397, 33.972.
The Tsezar Kunikov was sunk about 4 km off Alupka (44.420, 34.048) on Crimea's south coast, 43 km from Sevastopol.
Feodosia, at 45.034, 35.375, is a landing-ship berth where the Novocherkassk was destroyed in Dec 2023.
The reported wreck of the Sergey Kotov lies 5 km off Cape Takil (45.103, 36.453), which is 21 km from the Kerch Strait.

observations.subject: Cape Takil to the Kerch Strait, great-circle

text: The Crimean Bridge is at 45.279, 36.539 and was protected by Russian barricades.
The Kerch Strait, at 45.281, 36.549, is where the tanker Sig was hit (Aug 2023) and near where the Sergey Kotov sank.
Novorossiysk's Tsemes Bay, at 44.684, 37.841, has been the Black Sea Fleet's refuge since Oct 2023 and is 337 km from Sevastopol and 588 km from Odesa.
The Su-30SM shootdown of 2 May 2025 was about 50 km west of Novorossiysk.
The Ivan Khurs was attacked in the Bosphorus approaches, 120–140 km north-east of the strait and more than 400 km from Ukrainian waters; no source coordinate is given.
Sevastopol harbour was layered with nets, floating booms and a chain of barges against sea drones, as were other harbours and, after Jul 2023, the Kerch Bridge.
Budanov judged the defences of Sevastopol and Novorossiysk "comprehensive but [able to] be overcome", and preferred to catch Russian ships at sea, on duty or moving.
Ukraine's Black Sea corridor runs inside the territorial waters of Ukraine and its neighbours.
The first ship to use the Ukrainian corridor hugged the coast toward Romania.
The Magura developers say the Black Sea suits drone testing from late March to early November.
The Magura V5 handles up to sea state 2.
The Magura V7 handles sea state 3, with waves up to 1.25 m.
The Ivan Khurs mission started late because of bad weather.
Weather on the key nights of the Black Sea drone war is modelled from ERA5 reanalysis, and moon data come from USNO computed for central Crimea.
At about 04:00 on 29 Oct 2022 at Sevastopol, modelled weather was ENE wind about 10 km/h, cloud 50–100% and waves about 0.2 m.
On 29 Oct 2022 at Sevastopol the moon was 19% illuminated and set at 20:16, so the 04:00 raid was in the dark; sunrise was at 07:19.
On the night of 3–4 Aug 2023 at Novorossiysk, modelled weather was N wind 4–6 km/h, clear sky and waves about 0.05 m.
On the night of 3–4 Aug 2023 at Novorossiysk, a 90% moon was up all night (bright); sunrise was at 05:18.
On the night of 31 Jan – 1 Feb 2024 at Donuzlav, modelled weather was NW–W wind about 9 km/h, mostly clear, waves about 0.1 m and frost of −1 to −2 °C.
On the night of 31 Jan – 1 Feb 2024 at Donuzlav, a 65% moon was up until 10:47 (moonlit); sunrise was at 08:09.
On the night of 13–14 Feb 2024 at Alupka, modelled weather was NW wind 4–7 km/h, overcast with light drizzle, and waves about 0.5 m.
On 14 Feb 2024 at Alupka a 26% moon was not up until 09:59, so the pre-dawn attack on the Tsezar Kunikov was in the dark ("pre-dawn haze"); sunrise was at 07:45.
On the night of 4–5 Mar 2024 in the Kerch Strait, modelled weather was S–E wind 5–8 km/h, overcast, and waves about 0.1 m.
On the night of 4–5 Mar 2024 in the Kerch Strait, a 32% moon rose at 04:13; sunrise was at 07:04.
On 31 Dec 2024 off Cape Tarkhankut, modelled weather was W wind 17–19 km/h, overcast at night, and waves 0.5–0.7 m rising to 1.2 m in the evening.

observations.value_text: rising to 1.2 m in the evening

text: On 31 Dec 2024 off Cape Tarkhankut it was a new moon (0%); sunrise was at 08:29 and sunset at 17:16.
On 2 May 2025 west of Novorossiysk, modelled weather was N wind 18–25 km/h, variable cloud, and waves about 0.3 m.
On 2 May 2025 west of Novorossiysk a 27% moon set at 00:50; sunrise was at 05:19.
HUR (Defence Intelligence of Ukraine) is led by Lt. Gen. Kyrylo Budanov, and its spokesman is Andrii Yusov.
The head of HUR's unmanned-systems department is a general with the alias "Borets".
Group 13 is the HUR special unit that ran every Magura sinking and air kill; its commander's call sign is "Thirteenth".
HUR sea-drone operators sit at a "remote bridge" in Kyiv, over 1,000 km from the targets, for a day or two per mission, using two computers and a control panel.
HUR's sea-drone funding and support come through United24 and the Ministry of Digital Transformation.
The SBU is headed by Vasyl Malyuk, and a brigadier general called "Hunter" leads its Sea Baby programme.
The SBU ran the Sea Baby operations: the Kerch Bridge, Novorossiysk, the Sig, Samum, Derzhavin and Kozitsky strikes, and the Dec 2024 machine-gun raid.
Wikipedia names Brig. Gen. Ivan Lukashevych as the man who proposed SBU USVs; that he is "Hunter" is not established.
HUR says the SBU's Mamai long-range sea drone made the Novorossiysk hits.
The Ukrainian Navy co-planned the Novorossiysk, Sig and Sergey Kotov operations; its spokesman is Capt. 3rd rank Dmytro Pletenchuk.

The 385th Separate Brigade of Special-Purpose Naval Unmanned Systems was formed in Aug 2023 in the Ukrainian Navy, staffed mostly by HUR and SBU operators, and later came under the Unmanned Systems Forces.

text: At least 16 Magura V5s were seen at one base in Dec 2023.
A low-reliability source claims Magura V5 production of up to 50 a month.
35 Sea Babies were crowdfunded in Feb 2024 at about UAH 8.5m each.
Numbers of the SBU's Mamai sea drone are unknown.
Ukraine fitted its sea drones with R-73 "SeeDragon" missiles from 2024 and AIM-9M Sidewinders from Jan 2025.
Ukrainian Neptune, Harpoon and Storm Shadow strikes on Russian ships and the BSF headquarters shaped the Black Sea drone war.
Adm. Viktor Sokolov led the Black Sea Fleet until Feb 2024.
Vice Adm. Sergei Pinchuk was acting Black Sea Fleet commander from Feb 2024 and is named BSF commander in Dec 2024.
The Russian Navy commander-in-chief was Adm. Nikolai Yevmenov, then Adm. Aleksandr Moiseyev from Mar 2024.
Defence Minister Shoigu inspected the Black Sea Fleet on 17 Mar 2024.
Shoigu's successor Belousov inspected Black Sea Fleet naval-infantry training on 31 Dec 2024.
Pletenchuk says the Black Sea Fleet had about 80 units before the war.
Pletenchuk says that in Mar 2024 the Black Sea Fleet had left 10 missile carriers, 3 submarines, 2 missile boats, several patrol ships, and 5 large landing ships, 4 of them under repair.

observations.subject: BSF large landing ships under repair

text: The Ivanovets was a Project 1241.1 Tarantul-III corvette of the 41st Missile Boat Brigade: 56 m long, 41 kn, crew 40–45, armed with P-270 Moskit missiles and an AK-630M CIWS.
The Tsezar Kunikov was a Project 775 Ropucha-I landing ship of the 197th Landing Ship Brigade: 112.5 m long, 4,012 t full load, 17.6 kn, complement 87–98.
The Tsezar Kunikov was armed with 2×2 57 mm guns, Grad-M launchers and Strela MANPADS mounts.
The Sergey Kotov was a Project 22160 patrol ship: 94 m, 1,300–1,700 t, with an AK-176 76 mm gun and a helicopter deck, in service from Jan 2021.
The Olenegorsky Gornyak is a large landing ship of the Northern Fleet's 121st Landing Ship Brigade with about 100 crew.
The Ivan Khurs is a Project 18280 intelligence ship with a crew of 120, armed with 14.5 mm KPVT mounts and MANPADS.
Russia used Be-12 flying boats as spotters against Ukrainian USVs.
Russia's anti-USV forces included dedicated Mi-8 and Ka-27 helicopter units with rockets and machine guns, plus Ka-29 gunships.
Russia brought Mi-24VP helicopters from the Baltic Fleet's 396th Regiment to hunt Ukrainian USVs.
Russia used Su-30SM patrols and strafing against Ukrainian USVs.
Russia used Raptor patrol boats and KS-701 Tunets boats against Ukrainian USVs.
Russia used shipborne AK-630M guns and machine guns against Ukrainian USVs.
Russia used EW jamming against Ukrainian USVs.
Russia used FPV drones against Ukrainian USVs, launched first from boats and later from helicopters.
In Oct 2023 Black Sea Fleet ships moved to Novorossiysk.
Ryzhenko says that in Mar 2024 there were "no ships at sea for two weeks".

In 2024–25 Russian helicopters and jets hunted Ukrainian sea drones far offshore.

The Sea Baby has a 1,000 km range, and the 2024 model 1,000+ km.
The Magura V5 has up to 60 h endurance.
The Magura V7 has 48 h endurance, or 7 days with a generator, and carries 1,200 l of fuel.
The Magura V5 is rated for sea state 2.
The Magura V7 is rated for sea state 3, with waves to 1.25 m.
The Magura V5 uses mesh radio with an air repeater and/or SATCOM.
Two of the three dishes on the Magura V5 are reported to be Starlink terminals.

observations.subject: Starlink dishes on a Magura V5

text: After 2022 the Magura V5 got redundant communication channels.
The Magura V7 uses multichannel encrypted, EW-resistant satcom.
After the Starlink failure, the Sea Baby got several redundant links.
Magura V5 variants carry a ram warhead or two R-73 "SeeDragon" rails.
The Magura V7 carries two AIM-9M missiles on fixed pylons, or a machine-gun turret.
Sea Baby variants carry six RPV-16 thermobaric launchers, a heavy machine gun with auto-tracking, or mines.
The Magura V5 costs $273k according to Wikipedia, $250–300k according to a student journal, and "millions of hryvnias" according to HUR insiders.
A Sea Baby costs about UAH 8.5m, with UAH 297.5m raised for 35.
The Magura was designed "to intercept ships" at sea rather than in harbours, and is deployed for a specific mission, not constant patrol.
HUR sends Maguras in swarms of more than five drones, each with a place in the order of attack.

In a Magura swarm attack, the first strike immobilises the target, usually by hitting the engines or the stern; then the most vulnerable spot is hit; then follow-on drones are steered into the blast holes at the waterline before they detonate.
Ukrainian sea-drone attacks come at night, stern first, then amidships, to cause flooding and capsizing.
On the Ivanovets video, the drones zig-zag through AK-630M fire, and one hits where an earlier drone had torn a gash.
A low-reliability source describes a "chasing splashes" manoeuvre, steering a sea drone toward the last impact point to upset gunnery correction.
At the Ivan Khurs, the drone link dropped about 100 m from the ship; operators then shadowed the ship for about six hours, waiting for it to run out of ammunition, and struck at about 07:00.
When the intended convoy target moved hours before contact on 14 Feb 2024, the Magura swarm switched to the Tsezar Kunikov.
Sea Babies laid mines once booms blocked Sevastopol Bay; the SBU and WSJ say at least four ships were damaged.

observations.subject: ships damaged by Sea Baby mines

text: Magura V5s carried R-73 missiles from May 2024 (when first seen), with the first kill on 31 Dec 2024.
Air-launched, the R-73 has at least 30 km range and an 8 kg warhead.
Magura V7s carried AIM-9M missiles from Jan 2025; the hull turns to aim the missile horizontally, and the seeker's 60–67° field covers elevation.
The AIM-9M lacks the R-73's high off-boresight seeker, so the Magura V7 must point at its target.
Ukraine's mixed sea-drone swarms combine kamikaze boats, anti-air boats and gun boats.
European Security & Defence speculates that the 31 Dec 2024 Mi-8 kill used a lure, probably a feint toward Sevastopol.
A Russian analyst said of the 2 May 2025 Su-30 kill that Ukraine "lured it out and caught it".

cites.quote: lured it out and caught it

text: Booms, nets and barges were moderately effective against Ukrainian sea drones at harbour mouths.
Two USVs jumped the Sevastopol boom on 22 Mar 2023.
Aircraft were the main threat to Ukrainian USVs at sea.
Be-12 spotting aircraft cued Russian helicopters onto Ukrainian USVs.
A low-reliability source says Russian helicopters and jets "significantly reduced USV survivability in mid-2024".

cites.quote: significantly reduced USV survivability in mid-2024

text: A Ka-29 killed an R-73-armed USV in May 2024.
Russian EW jamming was moderately effective against Ukrainian USVs.
Russian ships moved in convoys with escorts and AIS switched off against Ukrainian USVs.
Russia launched FPV drones against USVs first from patrol boats, then from helicopters (Sep 2024).
Russian commentators say FPV drones "effectively destroy" USVs.
Russian ship self-defence failed against sea-drone swarms: the Tsezar Kunikov's crew fired back and manoeuvred "for a long time".
Milbloggers asked why the Sergey Kotov lacked anti-drone systems after three earlier attacks.

observations.subject: earlier attacks on the Sergey Kotov

text: UK Defence Intelligence judged Black Sea Fleet camouflage (black bows and sterns, painted decoys) unlikely to cut losses.
Relocation of the Black Sea Fleet to Novorossiysk, leaving the western Black Sea, was the decisive Russian counter to Ukrainian sea drones.
Before dawn on 29 Oct 2022, six to eight Ukrainian sea drones slipped into Sevastopol bay; one weaved among moored ships, U-turned and rammed a target.
On 29 Oct 2022 a sea drone hit the Grigorovich-class frigate Admiral Makarov, and the minesweeper Ivan Golubets was hit too; a boom in Pivdenna Bay was damaged.
The drone cameras in the 29 Oct 2022 Sevastopol raid cut out at impact.
Before the 29 Oct 2022 raid, Starlink failed over Crimea and the September 2022 sea-drone mission was lost.
In the 24 May 2023 attack on the Ivan Khurs, the drones made a 500 km transit, lost the link at 100 m, shadowed the ship under fire until morning, ran low on fuel, and scored a hit at the stern.
On 3–4 Aug 2023, under a bright moon, a 450 kg sea drone hit the Olenegorsky Gornyak in Novorossiysk Bay, and the ship was towed out listing at dawn.
Hours after the Novorossiysk strike, on 4 Aug 2023, the tanker Sig was holed off Kerch.
At Donuzlav on 1 Feb 2024, the Ivanovets was under way with its CIWS firing; drone 1 cut to the stern, drone 2 zig-zagged in, and drone 3 hit the existing gash.
The Ivanovets's ammunition detonated and the ship sank stern-first, bow up.

Off Alupka before dawn on 14 Feb 2024, the original convoy target slipped away, so the swarm turned on the Tsezar Kunikov; flashes were visible from the shore through haze, and holes opened along its port side.
Mi-8s and a Ka-27 circled after the Tsezar Kunikov attack.
In the Kerch approaches on 5 Mar 2024, the Sergey Kotov took five hits, a tow failed, and the Crimean Bridge was closed overnight.
Off Tarkhankut on 31 Dec 2024, helicopter gunfire splashed around a sea drone, which answered with an R-73; one Mi-8 pumped flares, was hit and fell into the sea, and a second limped home.
On 6 Dec 2024 the SBU's machine-gun Sea Babies fought in Kerch Bay.
On 2 May 2025, off Novorossiysk, three Magura V7s engaged a Su-30SM; an AIM-9 broke it up, and the pilots ejected and were picked up by a container ship.
In Sep 2022 Musk refused Starlink coverage around Crimea, and the first Ukrainian sea-drone mission failed.
In response to the Starlink refusal over Crimea, both Ukrainian sea-drone programmes (HUR and SBU) moved to redundant links.
Starlink terminals still appear on Maguras in later photos.
At the end of 2022, after disputes over quality, specification and budget, the SBU built its own Sea Baby and the original maker went to HUR.
The SBU–maker split produced two families of drones with different design briefs (static targets vs ships at sea), plus inter-agency rivalry.
HUR describes SBU and HUR operators refusing to share target coordinates, and says results were best when the agencies co-planned, as at Novorossiysk.
In 2023–24, Budanov chose to intercept Russian ships "on duty or being repositioned" rather than force the harbour defences at Sevastopol and Novorossiysk.
All three 2024 sinkings (Ivanovets, Tsezar Kunikov, Sergey Kotov) were of ships outside the main harbours.
Russia's move of the Black Sea Fleet in Sep–Oct 2023 followed the missile and USV strikes, including the 22 Sep 2023 strike on the BSF HQ.
Satellite imagery shows the Black Sea Fleet's shift to Novorossiysk in Oct 2023.
ISW credits Ukraine's 2023 campaign with "sequestering" the Black Sea Fleet in the eastern Black Sea.
Ryzhenko says the alternative base at Ochamchire was too small for the Black Sea Fleet.
In Aug 2023, after Russia had declared merchant ships hostile, Kyiv registered ships and sent the Joseph Schulte out on 16 Aug, opening its own corridor.
Ukrainian corridor volumes grew through 2024.
HUR's rule when a plan breaks mid-mission is not to interfere with the operators and to decide quickly; on 14 Feb 2024 the swarm switched to the Tsezar Kunikov.
Russia changed commanders in Feb – Mar 2024: Sokolov went after the Tsezar Kunikov sinking and Yevmenov after the Sergey Kotov sinking.
Shoigu ordered anti-USV drills and extra guns for the Black Sea Fleet in Mar 2024.
Russian milbloggers debated the "bureaucratic inertia" behind the Black Sea Fleet losses.
In 2024 Russia shifted to helicopters and Su-30SMs hunting Ukrainian sea drones offshore.
Budanov had already named air defence on the sea drones as "the next step" in Mar 2024.
R-73s were seen on Ukrainian sea drones in May 2024, and the first kill came on 31 Dec 2024.
In Jan 2025 HUR began fitting AIM-9s to sea drones and says "the best results [come from] the AIM-9".

cites.quote: the best results [come from] the AIM-9

text: Group 13 still plans R-73 fits as an alternative to the AIM-9.
After the May 2025 jet loss, Russian milbloggers argued for FPVs and ZALA–Lancet pairs instead of jets "firing cannons at USVs like in World War II".

cites.quote: firing cannons at USVs like in World War II

text: ISW records the Russian call for coastal FPV integration against USVs after the May 2025 jet loss.
Russia's own Katran USV is reported as a threat to Maguras.
On 29 Oct 2022, the Russian MoD admitted only "minor" damage to the Ivan Golubets and a boom, and said the ships guarded the grain corridor.
On 29 Oct 2022, Russia blamed British specialists in Ochakiv for the Sevastopol raid and suspended the grain deal.
The Russian MoD said "all three" boats that attacked the Ivan Khurs on 24 May 2023 were destroyed by gunfire.
Russia said the 4 Aug 2023 attack on Novorossiysk was "repelled".
On 14 Feb 2024 the Russian MoD said six USVs were destroyed, with no comment on the Tsezar Kunikov.
On 31 Dec 2024 Razvozhayev said 4 aerial and 2 naval drones were repelled, and did not mention the Mi-8.
On 2–3 May 2025 the Russian MoD claimed 170 drones, 11 missiles and 14 sea drones destroyed.
The Russian milblogger VoenkorKotenok confirmed the Ivanovets loss ("three hits from naval drones").
Aleksandr Kots confirmed the Sergey Kotov loss ("a story without a happy ending") and says the ship had repelled three attacks in Jul – Sep 2023.

cites.quote: a story without a happy ending

observations.subject: attacks on the Sergey Kotov repelled

text: Rybar confirmed the Su-30 loss of 2 May 2025 but says it was hit by an R-73, not an AIM-9.
In May 2025 Kotenok said the Black Sea Fleet is "huddled in harbors and bays" and that Ukraine has "an overwhelming advantage" in USVs.
HUR says most of the Tsezar Kunikov's crew died, while a former sailor told the BBC that all 89 were evacuated.

observations.subject: Tsezar Kunikov crew (former sailor to the BBC)

text: For the Sergey Kotov, HUR gives 7 dead, 6 wounded and 52 evacuated.
Russia's institutional reaction included sacking Black Sea Fleet commander Sokolov and Navy chief Yevmenov.
Russia's institutional reaction included Shoigu's anti-USV drills.
Russia brought in helicopter crews from the Baltic Fleet to hunt sea drones.
Belousov's Dec 2024 visit to the Black Sea Fleet stressed anti-UAV training for naval infantry.
An award was reported for the container-ship crew that rescued the Su-30 pilots in May 2025.
Russia has its own USVs: the KMZ "Dandelion" and the Katran.
HUR says Russian attempts to copy captured Maguras will lag behind.

counter: Magura V5 night swarm attacks (immobilise, breach, finish)
measure: Black Sea Fleet surface warships at sea
effect: three ships sunk in five weeks (Feb – Mar 2024); 5–6 hits needed per ship
rationale: Sections 1, 2 and 5: Magura swarms hunted ships at sea and sank the Ivanovets, Tsezar Kunikov and Sergey Kotov.

counter: harbour booms, nets and barge chains
effect: moderately effective at harbour mouths; on 22 Mar 2023 one USV stopped, two jumped the boom
rationale: Sections 2, 3 and 5: layered booms at Sevastopol and other harbours.

counter: hunting ships at sea instead of forcing harbours
measure: harbour booms, nets and barge chains
effect: all three 2024 sinkings were of ships outside the main harbours
rationale: Sections 3 and 7: Budanov judged harbour defences surmountable but chose to catch ships at sea.

counter: Sea Baby minelaying
effect: SBU and WSJ say at least four ships damaged by 15+ mines (SBU claim)
rationale: Section 5: Sea Babies laid mines once booms blocked Sevastopol Bay; first_observed is the Jun 2024 SBU report.

counter: uncrewed surface vessels (strike on the barricade)
effect: barricade destroyed
rationale: Section 2: barricade built Aug 2023, destroyed by USVs Nov 2023.

counter: anti-USV helicopters (Mi-8, Ka-27, Ka-29, Mi-24VP) with guns and rockets
measure: Ukrainian USVs in transit at sea
effect: aircraft the main threat to USVs at sea; a Ka-29 killed an R-73-armed USV (May 2024); 'significantly reduced USV survivability in mid-2024' (low-reliability source)
rationale: Sections 4 and 5: dedicated helicopter units hunted USVs offshore; first_observed is the Ka-29 kill footage.

counter: Su-30SM patrols and strafing
effect: jets hunted drones far offshore in 2024–25
rationale: Sections 4, 5 and 7: Russia shifted to helicopters and Su-30SMs.

counter: Be-12 maritime spotting cueing helicopters
effect: spotting cued helicopter interceptions
rationale: Sections 4 and 5.

counter: Magura V5 armed with R-73 'SeeDragon' missiles
effect: at least one Mi-8 downed off Cape Tarkhankut, HUR claims two; first air kill by a sea drone
rationale: Sections 1, 2, 5 and 7: Budanov named air defence on drones 'the next step' (Mar 2024); R-73 seen May 2024; first kill 31 Dec 2024.

counter: Magura V7 armed with AIM-9M Sidewinders
effect: at least one Su-30SM downed west of Novorossiysk, HUR claims two; hull must be turned to aim
rationale: Sections 1, 2, 5 and 7: AIM-9 fitting from Jan 2025; first jet kill 2 May 2025.

counter: Sea Baby with stabilised heavy machine gun
measure: Russian helicopters, Su-30 and Raptor boats hunting USVs
effect: SBU says helicopters damaged
rationale: Section 2, Kerch Bay raid of 5–6 Dec 2024 (SBU claim).

counter: lure or feint with anti-air sea drones in mixed swarms
effect: 'lured it out and caught it' (Russian analyst on the Su-30 kill); feint toward Sevastopol on 31 Dec 2024 is ESD speculation
rationale: Section 5: mixed swarms of kamikaze, anti-air and gun boats.

counter: shipborne AK-630M CIWS and machine guns
effect: failed against swarms: Ivanovets took six hits through AK-630M fire; Kunikov crew fired back without effect
rationale: Sections 2 and 5: ship self-defence failed against swarms.

counter: zig-zag evasion and 'chasing splashes'
effect: drones reached the target through CIWS fire; 'chasing splashes' from a low-reliability source
rationale: Section 5, Ivanovets video.

counter: shadowing a target until it runs out of ammunition
effect: hit near the stern after about six hours of shadowing
rationale: Section 5, Ivan Khurs chase.

counter: Russian EW jamming
effect: moderately effective
rationale: Sections 4 and 5.

counter: redundant multichannel links (mesh radio, satcom, encrypted EW-resistant satcom)
measure: Starlink refusal over Crimea and Russian EW
effect: both programmes moved to redundant links after the failed Sep 2022 mission; V7 satcom described as EW-resistant
rationale: Sections 2, 5 and 7, Starlink decision point.

counter: FPV drones launched from patrol boats and helicopters
effect: Russian commentators say FPVs 'effectively destroy' USVs
rationale: Sections 2 and 5; first_observed is the helicopter-launch training video.

counter: proposed coastal FPVs and ZALA–Lancet pairs
effect: proposed by Russian milbloggers after the Su-30 loss; not shown in use
rationale: Section 7, decision point 10.

counter: relocating the Black Sea Fleet to Novorossiysk and leaving the western Black Sea
measure: Ukrainian missile and USV strikes on Sevastopol-based ships
effect: decisive counter: fleet kept out of the western Black Sea
rationale: Sections 1, 2, 5 and 7.

counter: convoys with escorts and AIS switched off
measure: Ukrainian USV hunting of ships at sea
effect: no effect stated
rationale: Section 5.

counter: mid-mission retargeting
effect: swarm switched to the Tsezar Kunikov and sank it
rationale: Sections 5 and 7.

counter: black-painted bows and sterns and painted decoys
effect: judged unlikely to cut losses (UK DI)
rationale: Sections 2 and 5, Shoigu's measures.

counter: Ukrainian coastal export corridor
measure: Russian withdrawal from the grain deal and threat to treat merchant ships as hostile
effect: 45 Mt carried in about 9 months; April 2024 exports highest since Feb 2022
rationale: Sections 1, 2 and 7; lag from Russia quitting the grain deal (17 Jul 2023) to the first corridor sailing (16 Aug 2023).
